questions.q: Which statement is true of all living things?
o: They need food, water and air.
They can move from place to place.
questions.x: All living things need food, water and air, grow, respond and reproduce. Plants don't move from place to place, many animals have no lungs, and only plants make their own food.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a living thing?
questions.x: Fire uses air and spreads, but it cannot reproduce, grow from food or respond to changes like living things do. Mushrooms and yeast are fungi, and ferns are plants.

questions.q: Which characteristic shows that a mushroom is NOT a plant?
o: It cannot make its own food.
questions.x: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis, but fungi such as mushrooms cannot. Ferns also reproduce by spores, grow in damp places and have no flowers, so those don't separate fungi from plants.

questions.q: Which animal is a mammal?
questions.x: Mammals feed their young on milk and have hair or fur at some stage. A whale is a mammal that lives in water. A penguin is a bird, a shark is a fish and a crocodile is a reptile.

questions.q: An animal has six legs, three body parts and one pair of antennae. What is it?
questions.x: Six legs and three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen) define an insect. A spider has eight legs and two body parts.

questions.q: What property should the material for a frying-pan handle have?
o: It is a good conductor of heat.
It is a poor conductor of heat.
questions.x: A handle made of a poor conductor of heat, such as plastic or wood, does not get hot quickly, so it can be held safely.

questions.q: A window must let light through and keep rain out. Which material is most suitable?
questions.x: Glass is transparent and waterproof. Wood and aluminium block light, and cardboard soaks up water.

questions.q: Equal-sized pieces of materials W, X, Y and Z were each dipped into 100 ml of water and then removed. The water left was: W 60 ml, X 85 ml, Y 40 ml, Z 95 ml. Which material is best for making a mop?
questions.x: The best mop material absorbs the most water. Y left only 40 ml, so it absorbed 100 − 40 = 60 ml, the most of the four.

questions.q: Which animal has a three-stage life cycle?
questions.x: A cockroach goes egg → nymph → adult. Butterflies, mosquitoes and beetles have four stages: egg, larva, pupa, adult.

questions.q: In which stage of its life cycle does a butterfly eat the most?
questions.x: The caterpillar eats leaves constantly and grows quickly. The pupa does not feed at all.

questions.q: Which stage of a frog's life cycle lives only in water and breathes using gills?
questions.x: A tadpole lives in water and breathes with gills. The froglet and adult frog develop lungs and can live on land.

questions.q: A fruit is light and has wing-like parts. How is it most likely dispersed?
questions.x: Light fruits with wings or hairs are carried far by the wind. Fibrous, air-filled fruits float on water, and juicy or hooked fruits are spread by animals.

questions.q: What is pollination?
o: the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma
the joining of the male and female reproductive cells
the growth of a seed into a young plant
the movement of seeds away from the parent plant
questions.x: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma. Fertilisation is the joining of reproductive cells, germination is a seed growing, and dispersal is seeds moving away.

questions.q: In human reproduction, what happens during fertilisation?
o: A sperm fuses with an egg.
The egg is released from the ovary.
The baby develops in the womb.
Sperm are produced in the testes.
questions.x: Fertilisation is the fusion of a sperm with an egg to form a fertilised egg, which then develops in the womb.

questions.q: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.x: A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container. A solid has a definite shape and volume. A gas has neither.

questions.q: Water droplets form on the outside of a glass of ice water. Why?
o: Water vapour in the surrounding air loses heat to the cold glass and condenses.
The ice melts and evaporates out of the glass.
The cold glass gives off water vapour.
questions.x: Water vapour in the air touches the cold glass, loses heat and condenses into droplets. The water does not come from inside the glass.

questions.q: Which conditions will dry a wet towel the fastest?
o: folded, in the shade, no wind
spread out, in the sun, windy
spread out, in the shade, no wind
questions.x: Evaporation is faster with a larger exposed surface area, higher temperature and more wind.

questions.q: How are clouds formed?
o: Water vapour rises, loses heat and condenses into tiny water droplets.
Water in the sea boils and rises into the sky.
Smoke from factories collects in the sky.
Rain droplets freeze high in the sky.
questions.x: Warm water vapour rises, cools as it loses heat, and condenses into tiny water droplets that form clouds.

questions.q: A ball becomes heavier after more air is pumped into it. What does this show?
o: Air takes the shape of its container.
Air is a mixture of gases.
questions.x: The extra mass comes from the air pumped in, so air has mass.

questions.q: Which part of a plant carries water from the roots to the leaves?
questions.x: Water-carrying tubes transport water and mineral salts up from the roots. Food-carrying tubes carry food made in the leaves to other parts.

questions.q: A ring of bark, including the food-carrying tubes, is removed from a tree's stem. After a few weeks the stem just above the ring swells. Why?
o: Food made in the leaves cannot move down past the ring.
questions.x: The food-carrying tubes were removed, so food moving down from the leaves builds up just above the ring and the stem swells there.

questions.q: In which part of the digestive system is digestion completed?
questions.x: Digestion is completed in the small intestine, where digested food is also absorbed into the blood.

questions.q: What is the main function of the lungs?
o: to pump blood around the body
to take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
to remove water from the blood
questions.x: In the lungs, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide is removed. The heart pumps blood.

questions.q: In which of these parts does NO digestion of food take place?
questions.x: The gullet only moves food from the mouth to the stomach. Digestion happens in the mouth, stomach and small intestine.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
questions.x: The heart pumps blood through the blood vessels to all parts of the body.

questions.q: Which parts are found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.x: Plant cells have a cell wall for shape and chloroplasts for photosynthesis. Both cell types have a nucleus, cytoplasm and cell membrane.

questions.q: Which part of a cell controls all its activities?
questions.x: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell. The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves.

questions.q: In the circuit shown, switch S is open. Which bulb(s) will light up?
questions.x: The bulbs are in separate parallel branches. The open switch breaks only B's branch, so A's branch is still a closed circuit and A lights.

questions.q: Which object, placed across a gap in a circuit, will make the bulb light up?
questions.x: Steel is a metal, which is an electrical conductor. Rubber, plastic and wood are insulators.

questions.q: Two bulbs are connected in series to a battery. One bulb fuses. What happens to the other bulb?
o: It goes out, because the circuit is broken.
questions.x: In series there is only one path for the current. A fused bulb breaks that path, so no current flows and the other bulb goes out.

questions.q: Why can we see a book in a lit room?
o: Light from the book's own glow enters our eyes.
Light reflected off the book enters our eyes.
Light from our eyes falls on the book.
The book absorbs all the light.
questions.x: A book is not a light source. Light from a lamp or the sun reflects off the book and enters our eyes.

questions.q: The object is moved closer to the torch, as shown. What happens to its shadow on the screen?
questions.x: Closer to the torch, the object blocks a wider cone of light, so the shadow on the screen gets bigger.

questions.q: A metal spoon placed in hot soup becomes hot. Why?
o: Heat flows from the soup to the spoon.
Cold flows from the spoon to the soup.
Heat flows from the spoon to the soup.
questions.x: Heat always flows from a hotter object to a colder one, here from the soup into the spoon. There is no such thing as cold flowing.

questions.q: Why are small gaps left between sections of a railway track?
o: to allow the metal to expand when it gains heat
to make the train run more quietly
questions.x: Metal expands when it gains heat. Without gaps, the rails would push against each other and bend on hot days.

questions.q: A dented ping-pong ball regains its shape when placed in hot water. Why?
o: The air inside the ball gains heat and expands.
The plastic shrinks in hot water.
The air inside loses heat and contracts.
questions.x: Air inside the ball gains heat from the hot water and expands, pushing the dent out.

questions.q: Which are needed for photosynthesis?
questions.x: Plants use light energy, water and carbon dioxide to make food (sugar), giving off oxygen. Oxygen is a product, not a need.

questions.q: What are the energy conversions in a battery-powered torch?
o: chemical potential → electrical → light and heat
questions.x: The battery's chemical potential energy becomes electrical energy, which the bulb converts into light and heat.

questions.q: A ball is dropped and bounces. Each bounce is lower than the last. Why?
o: Energy is destroyed at each bounce.
Some energy is converted into heat and sound at each bounce.
questions.x: Energy cannot be destroyed. Some is converted to heat and sound at each bounce, so less is left to lift the ball.

questions.q: Which gas do plants give out during photosynthesis?
questions.x: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water and gives out oxygen.

questions.q: Which object will a magnet attract?
questions.x: Magnets attract magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt. Aluminium and copper are metals but not magnetic.

questions.q: The north pole of one magnet is brought near the north pole of another. What happens?
questions.x: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

questions.q: Which change makes an electromagnet stronger?
questions.x: More coils of wire (or more batteries) makes an electromagnet stronger. An iron core helps too. Plastic does not.

questions.q: The graph shows how the length of a spring changes with the mass hung on it. What mass makes the spring 16 cm long?
questions.x: The spring is 10 cm long with no mass and grows 2 cm for every 10 g. To reach 16 cm it must stretch 6 cm, which takes 30 g.

questions.q: Why do hiking shoes have soles with deep grooves?
questions.x: Deep grooves increase friction between the shoe and the ground, so the hiker is less likely to slip.

questions.q: Which force makes an apple fall from a tree?
questions.x: Gravitational force is the pull of the Earth on objects. It pulls the apple down.

questions.q: In the food web shown, all the frogs die. Which population will most likely increase at first?
questions.x: Frogs eat grasshoppers. With no frogs, fewer grasshoppers are eaten, so their population increases at first.

questions.q: A cactus has spines instead of broad leaves. How does this help it survive in the desert?
questions.x: Spines have a much smaller surface area than leaves, so less water is lost. They also protect the cactus from animals.

questions.q: Which is a direct result of clearing large areas of forest?
o: There is more oxygen in the air.
There is less carbon dioxide in the air.
There are more food sources for animals.
questions.x: Clearing forests destroys the homes of many organisms. It also leaves fewer trees to take in carbon dioxide.

questions.q: What is the role of decomposers such as fungi and bacteria?
o: They break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.
questions.x: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil for plants to use.
